Liya (Product): Heads-up: PrimeLedger reported a sudden throughput drop for embeddings on their Dedicated cluster after last night's "quant-mode" rollout. Support ticket #3129. Can we triage?

Nina (Support): PrimeLedger observes embedding QPS down ~60% and p95 latency up for small-batch requests. No errors, just backlog and longer queue times. Customer is on a 2xA100 dedicated pool.

Arjun (Eng Runtime): Noted. That rollout included the new int8-path + adaptive-kernel selection. deploy-bot shows rollout finished at 02:04 UTC.

deploy-bot: rollout completed: quant-mode-v2 (id: dpl-100122) 1: services: runtime, compiler-agent.

Priya (OnCall): I pulled metrics for pool PL-DED-2: token throughput dropped around 02:10 and concurrency per instance increased. No pod restarts. Model exec time down slightly, but queue_time spiked.

Ming (Eng Platform): Could be compilation cache miss leading to cold-path kernels slower initially. Check cache-hit metrics for compiled kernels and any high compiler latency.

Arjun (Eng Runtime): Checking compiler-agent logs: saw sustained compile latency bursts around 02:05-02:12 when many models requested int8 variants. Some instances fell back to the interpreter path for a few seconds while kernels compiled. That can explain increased queue time.

Nina (Support): Customer included a sample trace: shows ~900ms in "kernel_compile_wait" and ~150ms model. They said this affected a subset of tenants only.

Arjun (Eng Runtime): If compile happens inline on the request path for a cold kernel, queueing can blow up. We attempted async compile but config may allow inline fallback when cache miss >500ms. Need to know why async compile didn't trigger.

Priya (OnCall): I can check compiler-agent health and queue. The agent CPU was 100% for a short window at 02:06 on a couple of nodes. No OOMs.

Ming (Eng Platform): Our config has compile_concurrency=2 by default for Dedicated pools. For high model churn orgs that might be too low. Suggest immediate mitigation: increase compile concurrency for PL-DED-2 or pre-warm kernels for common models.

Carlos (Sales): PrimeLedger is pretty sensitive to throughput; they flagged a renewal conversation. Product needs a customer-facing plan quickly.

Liya (Product): Proposed steps: 1) immediate mitigation (raise compile concurrency, or temporarily pin quant-mode off for their org); 2) customer comms and ETA; 3) backlog: pre-warm kernels and better rollout gating for compiler changes; 4) define launch criteria for future quant/compile features. Agree?

Arjun (Eng Runtime): Agreed. Short-term: we can toggle org-level pin to disable quant-mode for PrimeLedger via control plane (non-disruptive) while we scale compile workers. I can prepare an ops action.

Priya (OnCall): I'll increase compile_concurrency to 6 for PL-DED-2 and watch. Will also tail compiler-agent logs.

Ming (Eng Platform): I'll add a dashboard alert for compile_wait > 200ms sustained and a metric for cache_miss_rate per pool. Backlog item: autoscale compile workers by pool traffic.

Nina (Support): I'll send PrimeLedger an initial update: "We see kernel compile backlog causing queueing; engineering will temporarily disable quant-mode for your org and increase compile workers; update within 90 minutes." Anything to add?

Carlos (Sales): Add: we'll schedule a postmortem with the account and include remediation timeline; ask if they want a short credit while we investigate.

Liya (Product): Good. Also add acceptance criteria for fix: pre-warm and autoscale should keep compile_wait < 150ms for 99.9% of requests in Dedicated pools. Rollout gating: require canary of compiled artifacts across 5% of traffic and observe compile_wait over 3 hours before global enable.

Arjun (Eng Runtime): Implemented org-pin toggle PR: https://git.redwood/d/pl/org-pin-quantmode (WIP). I'll coordinate with Priya to apply the toggle once compile_concurrency is increased.

Priya (OnCall): Increased compile_concurrency to 6 for PL-DED-2 at 02:28 UTC. Compiler-agent CPU now down and compile_wait dropping in metrics.

deploy-bot: feature-toggle applied: quant-mode disabled for org: primeledger (id: ft-7732)

Nina (Support): Customer update sent at 03:05 UTC: "We've temporarily disabled the quant-mode for your org and increased compile capacity; monitoring now. We'll provide a follow-up once fully validated."

Ming (Eng Platform): Creating backlog tickets (linking JIRA):
- ENG-PLAT-842: autoscale compiler workers per dedicated pool
- ENG-PLAT-843: pre-warm kernels for top-k models per org
- OBS-551: compile_wait alert and dashboard tile

Liya (Product): I'll own the product-side initiative to formalize rollout criteria for compilation/quant features and add a customer escalation playbook. Owners: Ming (platform), Arjun (runtime), Nina (support).

Carlos (Sales): I'll brief the account team and book a follow-up call. They asked for a postmortem and mitigation timeline for renewal discussion.

Arjun (Eng Runtime): Notes for RCA: 1) compile cache pressure from simultaneous demand for int8 kernels; 2) default compile concurrency too low for Dedicated churn patterns; 3) rollout lacked an org-level canary and pre-warming step.

Liya (Product): Thanks. Action items summarized: immediate toggle + scale applied; support to follow up with customer; Ming to create alerts and backlog; product to own rollout criteria + playbook; runtime to propose pre-warm design. We'll reconvene in 24h to review postmortem draft.

Priya (OnCall): I'll keep an eye on PL-DED-2 for the next hour and post any anomalies here.

Nina (Support): Closing initial incident thread in support, will reopen if customer reports further degradation.

Liya (Product): Closing internal triage for now; keep backlog items linked and prioritize the rollout checklist as P1 for next sprint. :white_check_mark:
